title: A signed-in user's language has one source of truth, `sys_user.locale` — the globe icon writes it and the i18n provider seeds from it (ruling batch #193 item 5 letter C on objectui#10051)

Path: none | 清单区 i18n:已登录用户的界面语言 | 一个词「语言」指两个设置:资料页写服务器、地球图标写本机,静默分叉
分诊重测与定级:2026-09-20T15:17Z

Filed by the director seat, summon #25 (`session_012GcsUbuqFGBibkEDMRC1eE`), executing ruling batch #193 item 5 letter C on objectui#10051 (maintainer 「其他同意」). ⛔ Filed bare: `domain:*`, `priority:*` and `type` are triage's production.

## The ruling this card executes

For a signed-in user, `sys_user.locale` (the column objectstack#14787 made writable, first written by objectui#7501's profile page) is the **single source of truth** for language. Today the profile page writes the server while the console's globe icon switches a device-local UI language, so one word 「语言」 names two settings that silently diverge: a user sets 日本語 in the profile and the UI stays English.

**Both halves land in ONE PR** (landing either alone leaves a transitional half-state):

1. **Provider seed precedence** (`packages/i18n`): signed in ⇒ the server's `sys_user.locale` seeds the UI language; the device value is the pre-sign-in fallback and a cache only; sign-out returns to the device value.
2. **The globe writes the server** (`packages/app-shell`): when signed in, switching the UI language writes `sys_user.locale` (reusing the write path objectui#7501 added) and updates the device cache; before sign-in it stays device-only. The profile page's language option and the globe therefore show the same value, and changing either changes both.

⛔ No rename of the profile option (D was refused, also as an interim). ⛔ The profile-page copy from objectui#7501's PR is untouched.

## Acceptance

- Pins: sign in with server `ja` on a device cached `en` ⇒ UI `ja`; globe switch to `de` while signed in ⇒ `sys_user.locale` reads `de` and the UI reads `de`; sign out ⇒ UI follows the device value; a fresh device with no cache ⇒ browser default before sign-in, server value after.
- A failed server write is **reported loudly** (the user sees it) and the local switch stands until the next successful read — ⛔ never a silent no-op.
- Notifications keep reading `sys_user.locale` (unchanged).
- `Clause-②` declared from the diff (a behaviour change on the published app-shell ⇒ expected `yes`); changeset per the packages' convention.

## Sequencing

Serial after objectui#9954 (in flight on `packages/app-shell`). Read objectui#10051's body for the four-facet analysis and the options refused.
